Either option is acceptable: remove the 44Ω resistors if they complicate the layout, or leave them in place if they are already fitted and not obstructing anything.

Those resistors on SDA/SCL are only there for signal quality. Because I2C lines are open-drain, releasing them requires the pull-up resistor to recharge the cable capacitance to 3.3V. That can produce slight overshoot or ringing at the transition edge, which the series resistance damps.

With our 20–40cm cables and 4.4kΩ pull-ups, rise time will remain well within specification, so this should not be a meaningful problem.

With the main board in the middle, the three boards are chained in this order: power board → main board → sensor board. Power reaches the main board from the power board through J\_PWR\_PWR, is consumed locally, and is also forwarded through J\_SENSOR\_PWR to the sensor board. It works like a power strip: power arrives through one cable, supplies the main board's own components, and continues to the sensor board via a second cable.
Immediately after the Schottky diodes, the INA219 sits in series on the 3.3V rail. It therefore measures the total 3.3V current for everything downstream—the ESP32 itself plus whatever the sensor board draws—in one reading.

Thanks, Luka. Everything is clear:
1. For v4, leave VRTC NC because this board has no external RTC chip. On the RTC topic, I realized that I previously mixed up VRTC with VBACKUP. VBACKUP (pin 27) supplies backup power to keep the AXP2101's internal RTC running after the main battery is removed. Could you expose VBACKUP on a small test pad or via beside PWROK from item #10? This would let us later install a 200 µF capacitor for \~8-10 min of hot-swap tolerance, a supercap for several weeks, or a CR1220 coin cell for \~9 years of real time-keeping. Nothing needs to be populated now; only expose the pad.
2. For the buttons (R16/R17/R18), agreed: convert all three to pull-ups at 3V3. They remain active LOW, with connector pin 1 tied to GND and a press shorting the GPIO input to GND. I updated <http://board-package.example|pcb-integrated.md> to reflect this.
3. The PIR (R19) and Touch (R20/R25) circuits are already correct as pull-downs and need no changes. Both the AM312 (PIR) and TTP223 (touch) provide push-pull active-HIGH outputs, so their internal drivers override the 20 k pull-down while active. The pull-down to GND simply ensures a defined LOW state whenever a sensor is unplugged.
